editorial.headline: The Work Behind a Well-Run Computer System
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers computer-systems advice, design and on-site management, open nationally to 100% foreign ownership and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This is the work of advising on, designing and helping run computer systems as an integrated whole. It includes guidance on the appropriate type, configuration and requirements of computer hardware and software; the point is not simply to recommend a product, but to make the system fit the operation it is meant to support. The activity also encompasses planning and designing systems that bring together hardware, software and computer communications technology.

That design work may be accompanied by system installation, training and user support. It can also extend into technical specifications and the procurement of system components, whether hardware or software, supplied directly or through a third party or vendor. The scope is therefore broad enough to accommodate both the advisory stage and the practical work of translating a technical plan into an operating environment.

It also covers managing and operating a client’s computer systems or data-processing facilities directly at the client’s premises, together with related support services. Software used on medical devices is specifically included among those related services. Registration is open at the stated micro, small, medium and large enterprise scales, making this an activity that can describe a compact specialist practice as well as a larger operation responsible for systems and facilities on behalf of clients.

Nationally, the activity is marked open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. Bali does not block PMA registration for it under the province-wide moratorium recorded here. That moratorium permanently blocks Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities for PMA across the island; for this activity, the OSS risk at the Large scale is Medium-High/High, and the record expressly identifies it as not blocked by the moratorium. The Bali position is therefore genuinely open on the facts provided: a foreign-owned business may register this activity there, rather than being excluded by the island-wide PMA restriction.
